name: Ariva ASVS 5.0 Level 2 gaps
description: Stories from the ARV-074 mapping (docs/security/asvs-l2.md): every Gap and Partly requirement belongs to exactly one story below. Not part of the Phase 0 count; schedule them with the product owner (most are hardening before a tender or a production go-live).

userStories.title: [ASVS] Data Protection key ring with RSA-OAEP and AES-GCM, and crypto agility
userStories.description: The key ring that protects refresh cookies, TOTP seeds and outbound secrets is wrapped by the framework's certificate encryptor with RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and AES-CBC without a MAC. Replace it with an encryptor using RSA-OAEP-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM, refuse weak certificates at startup, and make stored secrets re-protectable under a new key. ASVS 5.0: V11.3.1, V11.3.2, V11.3.3, V11.2.2, V11.2.3. Effort M.
acceptanceCriteria: A custom IXmlEncryptor and IXmlDecryptor wrap new keys with RSA-OAEP-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM; existing keys stay readable for migration; a test fails on rsa-1_5 or CBC in a written key
A Data Protection certificate under RSA 3072 (or an EC key under P-256) is refused at startup

Protected values carry their algorithm (the Data Protection key id and its descriptor); a job re-protects TOTP seeds and outbound secrets under the current key (credential hash labels moved to ARV-080a)

Give them one CredentialHash helper with an algorithm label (or an enforced rule that an unprefixed 64-character value is SHA-256 and anything else carries a recognised prefix), used by all four. Split from ARV-080. ASVS 5.0: V11.2.2. Effort S.
acceptanceCriteria: One CredentialHash helper formats and recognises the stored form for refresh tokens, recovery codes, device and display credentials; an unknown algorithm label is refused, with a unit test
Existing rows stay valid without a migration, or a versioned script migrates them; a test proves an existing hash still matches

userStories.title: [ASVS] No fail-safe on security decision caches
userStories.description: Session, role and site caches may serve a stale entry when the database is slow (fail-safe), so a revoked session or a removed role could pass during an outage. Turn fail-safe and soft timeouts off for every cache that feeds an authentication or authorization decision, as already done for the device credential. ASVS 5.0: V16.5.3. Effort S.
acceptanceCriteria: Every cache used for a session, role, site scope, integration client or display decision has fail-safe off and a hard timeout; an architecture test finds any security cache with fail-safe on
An integration test with the database stalled shows a revoked session refused (503), never accepted from a stale entry

userStories.description: Split from ARV-082 (2026-10-18). Production talks to PostgreSQL and Redis without TLS and could export telemetry in clear. ASVS 5.0: V12.3.1, V12.3.3, V12.3.4. Effort M.

PostgreSQL and Redis verify against a pinned internal CA (RootCertificate, sslCaPath), not the system store

The TimescaleDB chart serves TLS from a certificate secret and refuses connections without it when TLS is on; k8s-prd turns it on, and the platform chart mounts the database and Redis CAs in every host and job

userStories.title: [ASVS] Per-host database logins with least-privilege grants
userStories.description: Split from ARV-083. Every host shares one runtime database login. Give each host its own login, member of a role with only the grants it needs, starting with Ingest and Stream, and run the availability ledger job under its own login. ASVS 5.0: V13.2.1, V13.2.2, V13.3.2 (database part). Effort M.
acceptanceCriteria: One database login per host (api-main, api-ingest, api-stream, api-cronz, api-integration), each a member of its own role with grants limited to the tables and sequences that host reads or writes (derived from the code and checked by a test), created and granted by the versioned scripts and the migration job, never by SchemaUpdate

The availability ledger job (Ariva.Api.Cronz) runs under its own database login holding INSERT on availability_minute and INSERT and UPDATE on availability_cursor; the runtime login of every other host loses those rights, so a compromised host cannot record minutes ahead of the job or move a site's cursor past minutes (owner decision 2026-10-10, raised by the ARV-150 security review: the risk dates from ARV-118); an integration test as the runtime login shows both refused

An integration test logs in as each host's login and shows a write it does not need refused (at least: Ingest cannot write configuration tables, Stream cannot write accounts, every host but Cronz cannot write availability_minute or availability_cursor)
The chart gives each host its own database password secret and the hosts read only their own; the database-migration job sets automountServiceAccountToken: false

userStories.notes: Split from ARV-083 on 2026-10-18 (Effort L, three reviewable parts; the vault part needs the owner's choice of secret store). From ARV-083's notes: the database-migration job does not set automountServiceAccountToken: false (it needs no Kubernetes API access). 2026-10-10: owner folded the ARV-118 availability ledger rights into ARV-083 (now this story). 2026-10-19 (ARV-091 log inventory): the migration job sends the runtime login password in clear to PostgreSQL: SELECT ariva_ensure_runtime_login(@name, @password) (DatabaseMigrator.cs) binds it as a parameter, which the server logs with log_statement all or a duration threshold while log_parameter_max_length is -1, and the function EXECUTEs ALTER ROLE or CREATE ROLE ... PASSWORD %L, whose text a failing EXECUTE prints in the error CONTEXT. When the per-host logins replace this, send a SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier computed in the job (PostgreSQL stores a verifier given as the password as it is), never the password, and keep the advice of docs/security/log-inventory.md (log_statement none or ddl). ARV-096d (script 0063): each per-host login also gets the runtime statement timeout (ariva_set_runtime_statement_timeout, called by the migration job after the login is ensured), since a setting of a group role does not reach its members.

userStories.title: [ASVS] Ingress transport and header hardening
userStories.description: HSTS is not set (the controller default is six months), TLS versions and ciphers are not pinned, machine endpoints are redirected from HTTP silently, and responses the ingress generates itself lack the security headers. ASVS 5.0: V3.4.1, V3.4.4, V3.4.6, V3.3.1, V3.3.2, V4.1.2, V12.1.1, V12.1.2, V12.2.2. Effort M.
acceptanceCriteria: Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains on every host, and nosniff and frame-ancestors 'none' on ingress-generated responses, each with a chart test
The api-ingest, api-integration and api-main ingresses refuse plain HTTP instead of redirecting; the web and Cronz hosts keep the redirect
Controller ssl-protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 and Mozilla intermediate ciphers documented and shipped; MQTT pinned to TLS 1.2 and 1.3; a TLS check in the release gate
Ingress affinity cookies Secure and SameSite=Strict, the sidebar cookie Secure with a __Host- name
The deployment guide states which CA each host certificate must chain to; the TLS table in wiki 05 is current

userStories.title: [ASVS] Session management completeness
userStories.description: No per-account session limit, no credential rotation on step-up, no way for a user or an administrator to list or end sessions, and unattended tabs keep refreshing, so an open tab never idles out, a deviation from NIST SP 800-63B for every role that the documentation cannot justify (wiki 13 section 3, found in ARV-095). ASVS 5.0: V7.1.1, V7.1.2, V7.2.4, V7.3.1, V7.4.3, V7.4.5, V7.5.2. Effort L.
acceptanceCriteria: A configurable session limit per account with a documented behaviour at the limit
Step-up rotates the refresh token and starts a new session generation; earlier access tokens are refused
GET and DELETE api/auth/sessions (step-up) and an account screen listing device, address and times; administrator endpoints to end one user's or all sessions (step-up, audited)
After password change or recovery code regeneration the user is offered to end other sessions
Ariva.Web refreshes only after user activity, so the server idle timeout applies to unattended tabs (display players are unaffected)

userStories.title: [ASVS] Authentication secret hardening
userStories.description: Recovery codes have 50 bits and unsalted SHA-256, temporary passwords never expire, TOTP accepts the next step, per-request integration TOTP codes can be replayed, and the context word list is empty by default. ASVS 5.0: V6.5.1, V6.5.2, V6.5.5, V6.4.1, V11.5.1, V6.1.2, V6.2.11. Effort M.
acceptanceCriteria: Recovery codes of at least 128 bits, or stored with PBKDF2 and a per-code salt
Temporary passwords expire (for example after 72 hours); sign-in with an expired one fails
TOTP accepts the current and the previous step only, or the drift is documented; a per-request X-TOTP-Code is accepted once per step and client
A default context word list (Dalil, Ariva, AMAN, airport and authority names, role names) ships as Auth:ContextWords and is enforced by a test
Cronz and simulation keys documented as 32 random bytes with a generator command

userStories.title: [ASVS] No certificate downloads while a chain is built: Redis, and the collectors without a site CA
userStories.description: Found in the ARV-200 security review (M1, follow-up): the Redis connection's own chain check (RedisSettings.IsIssuedByPinnedCa in Platform/Backplane/Ariva.Infra/Caching/RedisConnection.cs) builds an X509Chain against the pinned CA without DisableCertificateDownloads, and the TLS handshake StackExchange.Redis runs before that callback builds a chain with the platform's default policy, which may download too. A party that can answer on Redis's address (a spoofed name, an on-path host) can present a leaf without its intermediate whose authority information access URL names an internal address, and the host fetches it during the handshake, before the peer is authenticated (CWE-918). The ARV-200 second review found the same for the collectors when no site CA is set: the Loki sink's own client and OpenTelemetry's default exporter clients use the platform's default chain policy, which on Linux fetches the issuer address a certificate names. Kafka and PostgreSQL to be checked the same way. ASVS 5.0: V12.3.2, V12.3.4. Effort S.
acceptanceCriteria: The Redis chain check and the handshake's own chain build download no certificate (DisableCertificateDownloads, through the client's SslClientAuthenticationOptions where StackExchange.Redis takes them, or a recorded reason where it cannot), with a test that a leaf whose intermediate is left out and whose issuer address is a loopback listener is refused and that the listener receives nothing, and a control that a chain allowed to download does fetch it
Without a site CA, Loki and the OTLP collector are still reached through clients that download no certificate (the public roots, with DisableCertificateDownloads), with the same test
PostgreSQL (Npgsql) and Kafka (librdkafka) are checked for the same behaviour and fixed or recorded with their evidence in docs/security/crypto-inventory.md (A15)

userStories.title: [ASVS] Brute force and lockout hardening
userStories.description: Found in ARV-095 (wiki 13 section 3, what waits for the login freeze): a right password without a code answers mfa_required and counts nothing, so credential stuffing learns which passwords are right; the per-account lock counts failures from any address with no window and can be used to keep known accounts locked; failures are not capped over time; a lock writes no audit entry or metric; unlock needs no step-up; the address limits are per process, IPv6 by full address, and sign-in shares one budget with refresh; open sessions survive a lock while /api/auth/me refuses it; an administrator can unlock their own account with a held session and guess step-up codes again. ASVS 5.0: V6.1.1, V6.3.1. Effort M.
acceptanceCriteria: A right password without a valid code answers and counts like any failure

The lock cannot be used to deny service to a known user (failures per account and source, or a delay that grows, instead of a hard lock), and consecutive failures are capped over time as NIST SP 800-63B section 5.2.2 asks
Every lock and unlock writes an audit entry and a metric; unlock is a critical action with step-up
Unlock refuses the caller's own account and needs step-up, with a test of the step-up, lock and self-unlock loop
Sign-in limits are shared across replicas (the Redis backplane), count IPv6 by /64 and give refresh its own budget
A lock applies the same way everywhere: open sessions and /api/auth/me treat a locked account alike, with tests

userStories.title: [ASVS] Secrets never in test reports or artifacts
userStories.description: From the ARV-104j security review (2026-10-11). Playwright uses an expect's custom message as the step title even when the assertion passes, and the HTML report keeps those titles; `expect(x.status(), await x.text())` therefore copies every answer body into the report. The live rehearsal's sensor registration put 20 device credentials into its report that way (fixed in ARV-104j, with an artifact check on the live-pipeline scopes). The same pattern is in 37 spec files, and CI uploads playwright-report (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so any spec whose successful answer carries a secret (a device credential, a display pairing secret, an integration client secret) leaks it into a CI artifact. Also carried here from the same review: the rehearsal's read-only database access with the runtime login instead of the owner, the observers' roles asserted in the live run, and separation of duties checked on both campaigns. Epic: Security. CWEs to review: CWE-532 (logging), CWE-287, CWE-863. ASVS: V13.3.1.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared E2E helper checks a response's status and puts the answer's body into the message only when the status is wrong; every spec uses it, and a test (or lint rule) fails when a spec passes a response body as an expect message

The artifact credential check of ARV-104j (`artifactCredentialCheck` in scripts/verify.mjs: plain files, the report's embedded zip and trace zips) also covers integration client secrets (ics_), JWTs and the run's E2E account passwords, runs after every Playwright scope of verify.mjs, and runs in CI before the report is uploaded; CI fails instead of uploading an artifact that holds one

The live rehearsal's read-only database access uses the runtime login (Database__Username) when it can read zone_outage, availability_minute, queue_bin and queue_minute; otherwise the reason is written in the spec and docs/harness/test-cadence.md

Before the simulator receives them, the live rehearsal reads the two observer accounts through the admin users API and asserts roles ValidationObserver only and sites DMO only; it checks that the campaign's manager is not among the observers on both campaigns, not only the first
